pairs.why: A keeps the real card's plain tone-on-tone stripe wall with no extra surface; B adds a floor ledge and a cast-shadow line the real card doesn't have.
Both swap the real card's soft light shafts and bubbles for a hard sunburst, but B adds a stronger glow halo that competes more with the hero, so A is slightly quieter.
B is a closer, simpler view with a few large shapes (posts, deck, sand, sky) and the dock dominant; A is a wide vista with a beach, clouds, many ripples and a reflection.
A's ground is a smooth dune under a sunburst, in line with the real cards' quiet surfaces; B scatters pebbles and speckle across the ground.
B has fewer props (just tree, path, a few bushes, tiny flowers), while A adds a city skyline, a large foreground bush and more flowers that the real park card doesn't have.
B's pi pattern is soft and tone-on-tone like the real card; A puts a bright glow halo behind the hero that pulls attention.
B has a quiet blurred park, with a few large shapes and the tree as the main backdrop; A adds a lamp post, bench, flowers, foreground leaves and a busy pink path.
